purpose: Freeze authoritative public evidence for dual-mode scramjet combustion-mode terminology, observables, transition mechanisms, and limitations before any LBW/YBW classifier or regime map is implemented. The project-specific meanings of the labels LBW and YBW are not inferred from the repository name and remain unresolved until a teacher/project source explicitly defines them.

evidence_sources.citation: Lu Tian, Lihong Chen, Qiang Chen, Fei Li, Xinyu Chang. Quasi-One-Dimensional Multimodes Analysis for Dual-Mode Scramjet. Journal of Propulsion and Power 30(6), 1559-1567 (2014).

supersonic_combustion_mode.isolator_state: Only very weak shock structures in the isolator.
supersonic_combustion_mode.flow_observable: Averaged Mach number remains above one along the engine duct in the authors' definition.

dual_mode_supersonic_combustion_mode.isolator_state: An obvious precombustion shock-train system is present.
dual_mode_supersonic_combustion_mode.flow_observable: Mach number behind the modeled precombustion shock train remains greater than one.

dual_mode_subsonic_combustion_mode.isolator_state: An obvious precombustion shock-train system is present.
dual_mode_subsonic_combustion_mode.flow_observable: Mach number after the modeled precombustion shock train is less than one.

subsonic_combustion_mode.isolator_state: Very strong shock structures may occur, potentially including a normal shock.
subsonic_combustion_mode.flow_observable: Averaged Mach number in the combustor is below one.

inlet_unstart.observable: The modeled precombustion shock-train length exceeds the available isolator length.

evidence_sources.project_use: Primary definition source for a future quasi-one-dimensional mode-state representation because it explicitly defines multiple dual-mode states and distinguishes the two dual modes by the state after the precombustion shock system.
evidence_sources.limitation: The paper includes a dedicated strength-adaptable precombustion shock model. The current project must not claim equivalent shock-train observability unless the solver/domain can represent and diagnose the isolator shock system.

evidence_sources.citation: Yan Zhang, Bing Chen, Gang Liu, Baoxi Wei, Xu Xu. Influencing factors on the mode transition in a dual-mode scramjet. Acta Astronautica 103, 1-15 (2014).

mode_taxonomy.pure_scram_mode: No pre-combustion shock train; combustion remains in the scram/supersonic family.
mode_taxonomy.dual_mode_scram_mode: A weaker oblique pre-combustion shock train is present while the one-dimensional averaged Mach number at combustor entrance is greater than one.
mode_taxonomy.dual_mode_ram_mode: A sufficiently strong normal-shock train in the isolator decelerates the flow to subsonic speed at the combustor entrance.

transition_observables: fuel equivalence ratio as a control/continuation parameter

facility_specific_example.condition: P0=0.85 MPa, T0=1200 K, isolator-inlet Mach 2.0, ethylene experiment described by the paper
facility_specific_example.lower_transition: Pure Scram -> Dual-Mode Scram; normalized wall pressure at x/H=2.5 reported as 0.23.
facility_specific_example.upper_transition: Dual-Mode Scram -> Dual-Mode Ram; normalized wall pressure at x/H=2.5 reported as 0.34.

evidence_sources.project_use: Supports a three-state experimental taxonomy and confirms that precombustion-shock structure plus combustor-entrance Mach are physically meaningful observables.
evidence_sources.limitation: The reported normalized-pressure values and equivalence-ratio transition points are facility/condition specific and must not be promoted as universal project thresholds. Hysteresis is reported in the transition region, so transition direction/history can matter.

evidence_sources.citation: Qili Liu, Damiano Baccarella, Brendan McGann, Tonghun Lee. Dual-Mode Operation and Transition in Axisymmetric Scramjets. AIAA Journal 57(11), 4764-4777 (2019).
findings_for_project: Mode-transition initiation depends on heat addition relative to area relief along the flowpath.
Thermal choking can be attained in a diverging combustor when combustion heat addition is sufficiently strong.
Thermal choking initiates near a pressure inflection where combustion heat loading and area relief become comparable in the reported configuration.
After scram-to-ram transition, steady ramjet combustion can be established upstream of the diverging section and the flow can subsequently reaccelerate to supersonic speed.
evidence_sources.project_use: Prevents a future classifier from treating downstream supersonic reacceleration as proof that the entire combustor is in scram mode; the relevant mode observable must be tied to the precombustion/combustor-entry state and transition topology.
evidence_sources.limitation: The paper does not provide a universal scalar threshold transferable to arbitrary project geometries.

evidence_sources.citation: Matthew L. Fotia, James F. Driscoll. Ram-Scram Transition and Flame/Shock-Train Interactions in a Model Scramjet Experiment. Journal of Propulsion and Power 29(1), 261-273 (2013).
findings_for_project: Ram-scram transition is associated with a sudden change in wall static-pressure distribution and flame position when the downstream boundary changes between choked and unchoked behavior.
A measured transition-boundary regime diagram was constructed rather than asserting one universal Mach-number threshold.
Low-frequency oscillations and coupling with the upstream precombustion pseudoshock can occur in part of the transition region.
evidence_sources.project_use: Supports explicit transition-region/uncertain classification and history dependence rather than forcing every state into a binary label.

evidence_sources.citation: Ruifeng Cao, Yue Lu, Daren Yu, Juntao Chang. Study on influencing factors of combustion mode transition boundary for a scramjet engine based on one-dimensional model. Aerospace Science and Technology 96, 105590 (2020).
findings_for_project: A one-dimensional model can be used to study a combustion-mode transition boundary.
The transition boundary depends on combustor area profile, heat-release distribution, wall temperature, wall roughness, and incoming-flow composition.
evidence_sources.project_use: Supports parameter-dependent regime mapping but explicitly argues against treating one threshold calibrated at one condition as universal.

frozen_general_rules.rule: Do not classify ram/scram family solely from the minimum Mach anywhere in the computational domain.
For dual-mode distinctions, the state of the precombustion shock system / isolator and the flow state near the combustor entrance are central observables in the cited literature.
Downstream reacceleration to Mach > 1 is compatible with ram-mode operation upstream and therefore cannot by itself establish scram mode.
Published wall-pressure or equivalence-ratio transition values are condition-specific unless a source explicitly establishes transferability.
A transition/uncertain band is scientifically preferable to a forced binary label when shock/flame oscillation, hysteresis, or insufficient observables prevent an unambiguous mode assignment.

search_record: The current repository contains no authoritative expansion or definition of the literal labels LBW and YBW.
The available prior project initialization material describes a scramjet/dual-mode quasi-1D CFD goal but does not define LBW or YBW.
Public exact-string searches did not recover a credible aerospace source defining LBW/YBW as standard dual-mode scramjet mode names.
project_label_resolution.policy: Do not map LBW or YBW to Pure Scram, Dual-Mode Scram, Dual-Mode Ram, supersonic combustion, subsonic combustion, geometry names, or any other state until an explicit teacher/project source resolves the labels.

blocking_items: Authoritative project-specific definition/expansion of LBW and YBW.
Explicit mapping from the project's modeled domain to the literature observables: isolator/precombustion shock state and combustor-entry Mach/state.
A decision on whether transition hysteresis/history is inside P11.3 scope or whether the first regime map is strictly steady/quasi-steady.
If wall-pressure thresholds are used, source-backed normalization and condition-specific calibration rather than copying Zhang et al.'s facility-specific 0.23/0.34 values.
